amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

## Summary

The bug was in `Replacer::replace_all` in `crates/printer/src/util.rs`. In multiline mode, the replacement machinery extends the subject by up to `MAX_LOOK_AHEAD` bytes past the end of the reported match range (a kludge to support regex look-ahead, mirroring `find_iter_at_in_context`). The rewritten replacement loop:

1. never rejected matches that begin at or after `range.end`, so matches living entirely in the look-ahead region were found and replaced too, and
2. copied the trailing unmatched tail all the way to `subject.len()` instead of stopping at `range.end`, dragging look-ahead bytes into the printed replacement.

Fix (crates/printer/src/util.rs):
- Break out of the match loop when `match_start >= range.end`, mirroring the check `find_iter_at_in_context` already applies for non-replacement searching.
- Bound the final tail-copy to `min(subject.len(), range.end)` (extending to `subject.len()` only when the last match legitimately ended past `range.end`).

Verification:
- `regression::r2208` and `regression::r2095` (the FAIL_TO_PASS cases) now pass.
- Full workspace suite: 924 tests, 0 failures (all PASS_TO_PASS cases intact).
- Manual repro of the issue's exact command now prints only ` [-h] [-U|-u <pkgspec>[,<pkgspec>...]] [<reqs-in>...] [-- <pip-compile-arg>...]`.
